tests.title: Unit 1: Introduction to Management – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: A manager spends most of the day setting targets, deciding who will do what and checking progress against targets. Which set of management functions is she performing?
options: Staffing, directing and coordinating
Forecasting, motivating and appraising
Planning, organising and controlling
Budgeting, recruiting and training
questions.explanation: Targets, allocation of tasks and checking progress.

questions.question_text: Which statement best captures the difference between efficiency and effectiveness in management?
options: Efficiency is doing things right; effectiveness is doing the right things
Efficiency is setting the goals; effectiveness is using the resources
Efficiency is about the long run; effectiveness is about the short run
Efficiency is about the people; effectiveness is about the profit

questions.question_text: A manager reduces wastage and produces the same output with fewer inputs, but the product no longer sells in the market. The manager is:
options: Both efficient and effective
Neither efficient nor effective
Effective but not efficient
Efficient but not effective
questions.explanation: Output is wasted if no demand.

questions.question_text: Which feature of management is shown by the statement "management is needed in a school, a hospital and a factory"?
options: Intangibility
Continuous process
Multi-dimensional nature
Universality

questions.question_text: Management is described as intangible because:
options: It does not need any scientific knowledge or training for its practice in a business
It cannot be seen, though its results are felt in performance
It is practised only by the top level of the organisation, which is not visible to others
It applies to profit-making organisations only and not to the social ones

questions.question_text: Which of the following best shows management as an art?
options: Having a well-defined body of principles tested by experiments
Being governed by a code of conduct enforced by an association
Requiring a formal degree for entry into the profession
Applying personal skill and creativity to use theory in practice

questions.question_text: Management does not fully qualify as a profession mainly because:
options: Entry to it is not restricted by a prescribed degree
Managers do not render service to any group of persons in the society
Managers have no knowledge base on which to rely in their work as managers
Managers are not paid any price or fee for the managerial services they render

questions.question_text: F. W. Taylor is best known for:
options: Human relations
Administrative management
Scientific management
Contingency approach

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT one of Taylor's principles?
options: Unity of command
Cooperation, not individualism
Harmony, not discord
Science, not rule of thumb

questions.question_text: Taylor's "functional foremanship" meant:
options: Dividing supervision of a worker among eight specialist foremen
Making one foreman responsible for all the activities of workers
Letting workers choose their own supervisors
Giving the foremen no role in planning

questions.question_text: Under Taylor's differential piece rate system, a worker who exceeds the standard output is paid:
options: A higher rate per unit for all the units produced
A lower rate per unit for the units above the standard
The same rate per unit as the others who meet the standard
A fixed salary irrespective of the units produced

questions.question_text: Time study, motion study and fatigue study are techniques associated with:
options: Administrative management
Human relations movement
Scientific management
Systems approach

questions.question_text: Henri Fayol's main contribution was that he:
options: Introduced time and motion study at the shop-floor level of the factories
Proposed the Theory X and Theory Y assumptions about the worker
Identified 14 general principles of management
Conducted the Hawthorne experiments on the worker behaviour at a plant

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a Fayol principle that suggests "a subordinate should receive orders from only one superior"?
options: Scalar chain
Unity of direction
Unity of command
Centralisation

questions.question_text: "One head and one plan for a group of activities having the same objective" describes:
options: Unity of command
Unity of direction
Order
Division of work

questions.question_text: Fayol's scalar chain refers to the:
options: Series of steps followed in the process of decision making
Chain of suppliers who deliver materials to the manufacturing firm
Sequence of operations on an assembly line in a factory
Chain of authority from the top level to the lowest level

questions.question_text: A "gang plank" in Fayol's scalar chain allows:
options: Managers to avoid reporting to higher levels
Employees at the same level to communicate directly in an emergency
Employees to appeal to outside authorities against their managers
Employees to bypass the top management for promotions

questions.question_text: Which of the following Fayol principles is similar to Taylor's idea of "harmony, not discord"?
options: Remuneration
Esprit de corps
Order
Centralisation

questions.question_text: The Hawthorne experiments showed that workers' productivity was influenced mainly by:
options: Physical working conditions such as lighting and temperature
Machines and technology used in the plant
Social and psychological factors such as attention and group norms
Wages paid under the differential piece rate system

questions.question_text: The human relations approach, in contrast with scientific management, emphasises:
options: Mathematical models for decision making
Hierarchy and rules as a basis of control
Employees as social beings with needs beyond pay
Standardisation of tools and working methods

questions.question_text: The contingency approach says that:
options: The environment has no influence on organisation design
The same principles apply to all organisations in all situations
There is no one best way of managing; it depends on the situation
Managers should rely on rules and not on judgement

questions.question_text: The systems approach views an organisation as:
options: An independent entity with no dealings with outsiders
A hierarchy of positions arranged by authority levels
A set of interrelated parts that interact with the environment
A collection of individuals each pursuing personal goals

questions.question_text: The top level of management is mainly concerned with:
options: Supervising the daily work of operatives
Framing overall objectives and policies
Implementing the decisions of the middle level
Training workers in routine operations

questions.question_text: The middle level of management mainly:
options: Formulates the overall mission and long-term strategy for the whole firm
Interprets policies and passes plans to supervisors
Directly supervises the operating workers on the shop floor of the firm
Works only on the long-term financial planning of the organisation
questions.explanation: Link between top and lower levels.

questions.question_text: First-line managers are best described as those who:
options: Directly supervise operating employees
Represent the shareholders on the Board
Interpret company policies for departments
Make decisions about the firm's long-term goals

tests.title: Unit 1: Introduction to Management – Practice Test 2

questions.question_text: Which skill is relatively more important for top-level managers than for first-line managers?
options: Technical skills
Operational skills
Manual skills
Conceptual skills
questions.explanation: Seeing the organisation as a whole.

questions.question_text: Technical skill is most important for:
options: Shareholders
Board of Directors
Top managers
First-line managers

questions.question_text: "The ability to work with people and motivate them" is called:
options: Technical skill, needed mostly at the lowest levels only
Human or interpersonal skill, needed at all the levels
Conceptual skill, needed mostly at the top levels only
Analytical skill, needed mostly by the specialists only

questions.question_text: Mintzberg classified managerial roles into:
options: Planning, organising and controlling
Strategic, tactical and operational
Technical, human and conceptual
Interpersonal, informational and decisional

questions.question_text: When a manager acts as a spokesperson to the media on behalf of the firm, which Mintzberg role is it?
options: Informational — spokesperson
Interpersonal — figurehead
Decisional — negotiator
Decisional — entrepreneur

questions.question_text: A manager resolves a dispute between two departments. The Mintzberg role is:
options: Disturbance handler
Monitor
Figurehead
Liaison

questions.question_text: A manager attends the wedding of an employee as the representative of the firm. The role is:
options: Figurehead
Resource allocator
Leader
Negotiator

questions.question_text: Coordination is called the essence of management because it:
options: Is a separate function distinct from planning and organising
Is needed only when the firm is in a crisis
Brings together the efforts of people and departments towards common objectives
Is performed only by managers at the top level of the organisation

questions.question_text: Which feature of coordination is revealed by "it is needed at all levels of management"?
options: Continuous
Pervasive
Deliberate
Separate function

questions.question_text: Management by Objectives (MBO) was popularised by:
options: Peter Drucker
Elton Mayo
F. W. Taylor
Henri Fayol

questions.question_text: In MBO, objectives are set:
options: By external consultants for the entire firm
Jointly by the superior and the subordinate
By the top management alone for all employees
By the employees without involving managers

questions.question_text: A manager's primary responsibility towards shareholders is:
options: Producing goods at the lowest cost
Reducing prices for the consumers
Providing employment in the area
Earning a fair return on investment

questions.question_text: "Social responsibility of business" means that a business should:
options: Consider the interests of society along with its own profit
Maximise short-term profit without regard to social issues
Leave social problems to the government completely
Donate all its profits to charity each year

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of an organisation's social objective?
options: Introducing a new product line
Increasing the market share by ten per cent
Raising return on investment
Providing quality goods at reasonable prices

questions.question_text: An organisation sets a target of increasing its share in the market from 20% to 25% within two years. This is an example of:
options: A human objective
A personal objective
An economic objective
A social objective

questions.question_text: The statement "management is a goal-oriented process" suggests that:
options: Management has no connection with the organisation's goals
Management is required only when goals are not clear
Management and goals are dealt with by different persons
Management is aimed at achieving the objectives of the organisation

questions.question_text: Fayol's principle of "equity" implies that:
options: Every employee should be given equal work and equal rank
Authority and responsibility should be kept equal
All employees should be paid exactly the same wages
Managers should treat employees with kindness and justice

questions.question_text: Fayol's "stability of tenure of personnel" means that:
options: Managers should be fixed in one post until retirement
Employees should be transferred every year to avoid boredom
Employees should not be moved frequently, as frequent turnover is costly
Employees should be given permanent jobs irrespective of performance

questions.question_text: "Authority and responsibility must be equal" is a principle of:
options: Mayo
Drucker
Taylor
Fayol

questions.question_text: Fayol's principle of "initiative" encourages:
options: Customers to give suggestions to the firm
Employees to think out and carry out a plan
Managers to take all the decisions on their own
Employees to follow instructions without questioning

questions.question_text: The "span of control" in an organisation refers to:
options: The number of subordinates a manager can effectively supervise
The geographical area covered by the firm's operations
The time within which a project must be completed
The range of products manufactured by the firm
questions.explanation: Not a Fayol principle, but a management concept.

questions.question_text: Which approach is described as "the one best way to do a job is found by scientific investigation"?
options: Contingency approach
Quantitative approach
Scientific management
Behavioural approach

questions.question_text: Scientific management has been criticised mainly because it:
options: Gave too much importance to human relations in the workplace
Ignored the problems of productivity in industries
Treated workers as machines and ignored their social needs
Failed to introduce any standard methods of work

questions.question_text: Fayol's approach is mainly criticised for:
options: Treating the principles as universal, whatever the situation
Having no practical application in the business organisations of today
Concentrating on the shop floor and ignoring the top management levels
Being based on laboratory experiments carried out in a factory

questions.question_text: The best way to describe the difference between Taylor and Fayol is:
options: Taylor studied the top management; Fayol studied the shop floor
Taylor was only a theorist; Fayol was only a practising engineer
Taylor studied the human side; Fayol studied the technical side
Taylor studied the shop floor; Fayol studied the whole organisation

tests.title: Unit 1: Introduction to Management – Practice Test 3

questions.question_text: Taylor's principle of "science, not rule of thumb" implies:
options: Using intuition to decide the standard time for jobs
Replacing guesswork with careful study of each element of a job
Relying on the experience of the old workers to decide methods
Letting each worker decide how to carry out the work

questions.question_text: "Mental revolution" in Taylor's scheme means a change in the attitude of:
options: Both workers and management towards each other
Management alone towards workers' demands
Workers alone towards the new methods of working
Customers towards the products of the organisation

questions.question_text: The organisation of the military uses which of Fayol's ideas strongly?
options: Initiative and esprit de corps
Stability of tenure and order
Scalar chain and unity of command
Remuneration and equity

questions.question_text: The "gang plank" is an exception to which principle?
options: Centralisation
Unity of command
Order
Scalar chain

questions.question_text: In the context of Fayol's "centralisation and decentralisation", the optimum degree depends on:
options: The wishes of the owners and shareholders
The age of the firm since its incorporation
The size of the firm and the situation it faces
The number of products made by the firm

questions.question_text: Which of these is a feature of management as a "science"?
options: Principles derived from experiments and observation
Total exactness and predictability of results
Absence of any cause-and-effect relationship
Principles based only on the personal skill of managers

questions.question_text: "Management is a dynamic function" means that:
options: Management is concerned with the movement of goods
Management must adapt itself to changes in the environment
Management has a fixed set of principles that never change
Management is the job of the dynamic leaders alone

questions.question_text: An organisation's vision statement is usually concerned with:
options: The list of products sold at present
The details of the profit for the current year
Where the organisation wants to be in the long run
How the organisation will carry out its daily operations

questions.question_text: A mission statement describes:
options: The structure of the departments in the firm
The purpose for which the organisation exists
The accounts of the organisation at the year end
The day-to-day tasks of the employees in departments

questions.question_text: Which of these is a human or employee-related objective of an organisation?
options: Providing fair wages and better working conditions
Earning a better return for the owners
Contributing to the national economy
Supplying quality goods to the consumers

questions.question_text: Peter Drucker said that the primary task of a manager is to:
options: Reduce the cost of production
Maximise the profit in the short run
Supervise every activity in detail
Make people capable of joint performance

questions.question_text: The difference between management and administration, as given by Oliver Sheldon, is that administration:
options: Deals only with government organisations, management with business
Determines the objectives and policies, and management executes them
Has no relation to the policies of the organisation
Executes the policies, and management determines them

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of a "decisional" role of a manager?
options: Reading industry reports for market news
Writing a letter of thanks to a customer
Giving a speech at a college function
Allocating a budget between departments

questions.question_text: A manager scans journals and market reports to find new trends. Which Mintzberg role is it?
options: Disseminator
Monitor
Spokesperson
Leader

questions.question_text: A manager hires the best candidates and motivates the team. Which role?
options: Liaison
Leader
Negotiator
Figurehead

questions.question_text: Management is "universal" in the sense that:
options: Its basic principles apply to all organisations, though practice differs
Management is the same in every detail in all types of organisations
Management is found only in large business organisations of the country
Management is a function performed only by the owners of the business

questions.question_text: The main reason for studying the principles of management is to:
options: Obtain exact answers to every managerial problem that arises daily
Understand guidelines that help managers in taking decisions
Memorise the rules for the preparation of the accounts of a business
Learn the laws that are made by the government for the business firms

questions.question_text: Principles of management differ from the principles of pure science because they are:
options: Free from the influence of human behaviour
Applicable only in physical sciences
Always exact and not changing with time
Flexible and dependent on the situation

questions.question_text: Taylor's standardisation and simplification of work aims at:
options: Fixing standard tools, methods and working conditions
Allowing each worker to use the tools of his own personal choice
Making every job complex enough that it needs a skilled worker
Removing all specialisation among the workers on the shop floor

questions.question_text: In which situation is the differential piece-wage system MOST likely to motivate?
options: Workers have no way of knowing the standard output
Workers fear losing their jobs by performing well
Workers are paid a fixed monthly salary regardless of output
Workers believe that extra effort will be fairly rewarded

questions.question_text: The statement "no man can serve two masters" is most closely associated with:
options: Unity of direction
Division of work
Scalar chain
Unity of command

questions.question_text: Subdividing work into specialised tasks to increase output best describes:
options: Equity
Division of work
Discipline
Order

questions.question_text: The principle of "discipline" in Fayol's list implies:
options: Obedience and respect for the agreed rules of the organisation
Punishment of employees for even small mistakes
Total freedom for employees to follow their own rules
Strict control by managers over every employee action

questions.question_text: "A place for everything and everything in its place" illustrates Fayol's principle of:
options: Scalar chain
Initiative
Order
Equity

questions.question_text: The subordination of individual interest to general interest requires that:
options: Managers sacrifice their own interest and not employees'
Personal goals are to be ignored in all situations
The goals of the employees prevail over the organisation's
The goals of the organisation prevail over personal goals

tests.title: Unit 1: Introduction to Management – Practice Test 4

questions.question_text: An organisation requires a manager to supervise 50 workers at a time. Which principle is likely to be violated?
options: Discipline
Division of work
Span of control
Unity of command

questions.question_text: Which of the following BEST illustrates the use of the scientific approach in a call centre?
options: Measuring the time per call and fixing a standard handling time
Relying on the judgement of the oldest agent for targets
Letting each agent decide the time to be spent on each call
Rewarding agents by seniority and not by performance

questions.question_text: Which of the following would be a human-relations approach to increase productivity in the same call centre?
options: Recognising the employees' work and giving them a voice in the decisions
Increasing the number of calls per hour expected from each agent
Installing software that monitors each call in real time
Cutting the break time to increase the available working hours

questions.question_text: A restaurant owner changes the menu, hours and prices after a new competitor opens nearby. This best illustrates the:
options: Administrative approach
Contingency approach
Scientific management approach
Bureaucratic approach

questions.question_text: A firm views its marketing, finance and production departments as parts that depend on each other. This is the:
options: Quantitative approach
Scientific approach
Systems approach
Behavioural approach

questions.question_text: The quantitative (management science) approach uses:
options: Detailed study of the firm's history to guide decisions
Mathematical models and statistics to solve managerial problems
Rules of thumb collected from the experienced managers
Observation of group behaviour to resolve conflicts

questions.question_text: Which of these is a characteristic of a 'profession'?
options: Absence of a formal body of specialised knowledge
Open entry for anyone willing to take up the work
A code of conduct and an association that regulates entry
Service aimed only at the profit of the practitioner

questions.question_text: Which among these is the correct order of management levels from top to bottom?
options: Top, first-line, middle
Top, middle, first-line
Middle, top, first-line
First-line, middle, top

questions.question_text: Mintzberg's "liaison" role involves:
options: Giving formal speeches at ceremonies of the firm
Maintaining a network of contacts outside the organisation
Handling the crises that arise in the organisation
Deciding how the resources of the firm are to be shared

questions.question_text: The functions of management according to Koontz and O'Donnell are:
options: Production, marketing, finance and personnel management
Coordination, communication, recruitment and training of staff
Forecasting, auditing, costing and budgeting of operations
Planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling

questions.question_text: Henri Fayol's five elements of management include:
options: Forecasting, auditing, budgeting, costing and reporting
Planning, staffing, directing, motivating and leading
Planning, organising, commanding, coordinating and controlling
Production, finance, marketing, personnel and accounting

questions.question_text: Productivity is measured as:
options: Sales per employee only
Profit per unit of sales
Input per unit of output
Output per unit of input

questions.question_text: A firm increases output from 500 to 600 units using the same 100 labour hours. Productivity of labour has risen from:
options: 5 to 6 units per hour
5 to 6 hours per unit
6 to 5 units per hour
500 to 600 hours

questions.question_text: The environment of a business that includes customers, competitors and suppliers is the:
options: Legal environment
Internal environment
Micro or task environment
Macro or general environment

questions.question_text: A change in government policy on taxation is part of the:
options: Competitor analysis
Macro or general environment
Task environment
Internal environment

questions.question_text: Which statement about "levels of management" is TRUE?
options: The first-line managers frame the policies of the organisation
As we move up, the decisions become more strategic and long-term
The top managers supervise the daily work of the workers
As we move up, the decisions become more routine and short-term

questions.question_text: The idea that managers should balance the interests of employees, customers and shareholders reflects:
options: A scientific approach
A bureaucratic approach
A shareholder-only approach
A stakeholder approach

questions.question_text: Which of these is a likely result of poor coordination?
options: Better use of the resources of the organisation
Greater morale among the employees of the firm
Duplication of work and conflicts between departments
Higher output with lower costs in the departments

questions.question_text: A newly appointed manager discovers that sales, production and purchase teams are working at cross-purposes. The management function most needed is:
options: Auditing
Staffing
Budgeting
Coordination

questions.question_text: Management is called a "continuous process" because its functions:
options: Go on repeatedly as long as the organisation lasts
End once the plans of the organisation have been completed
Are required only when a new organisation is started up
Are required only at times of crisis in the organisation

questions.question_text: Effective managers are those who achieve goals:
options: By using resources in the best possible manner
Using the maximum resources available
Without any regard for the cost involved
Only through close personal supervision

questions.question_text: Peter Drucker identified key result areas such as:
options: Recruiting, training, promoting, transferring and dismissing
Accounting, auditing, costing, budgeting and reporting
Planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling
Market standing, innovation, productivity and profitability

questions.question_text: A criticism of the human relations approach is that it:
options: Overstressed worker satisfaction and neglected the structure
Laid too much stress on time and motion study of the workers
Ignored the social needs of the employees at the workplace entirely
Was concerned only with the top management of the organisation

questions.question_text: The behavioural approach to management draws mostly on:
options: Mathematics and statistics
Psychology and sociology
Law and political science
Engineering and physics

questions.question_text: The idea of "management as a process" is best shown by:
options: A single decision taken once by the top management of the firm
The ownership of capital by the shareholders of the company
Planning, organising, directing and controlling in sequence
The production of goods in a factory by the workers of the firm
